subject: Computer Science
summary: Covers how the web works (HTTP, URLs, servers, hosting), HTML and HTML5, CSS selectors and layout, JavaScript with the DOM event model, XML with DTD/Schema and parsers, front-end tools and the Microsoft .NET/ASP.NET platform. DSSSB asks many one-line fact questions here: tag attributes, CSS property names, event names, XML rules and .NET full forms.

sections.heading: How the web works: client, server, HTTP and URL
sections.body:
The web is a **client-server** system. A browser (client) sends an **HTTP request** to a web server, which returns an **HTTP response** (HTML, CSS, JS, images, JSON). HTTP is an application-layer, **stateless** protocol: each request is independent, so state is kept with **cookies**, **sessions** or tokens. Default ports: HTTP **80**, HTTPS **443** (HTTP over TLS/SSL).

A **URL** (Uniform Resource Locator) gives the location of a resource: `scheme://host:port/path?query#fragment`, e.g. `https://www.example.com:443/notes/index.html?id=5#top`. **DNS** translates the host name into an IP address.

- **HTTP methods**: GET (fetch; data in URL, bookmarkable, length-limited), POST (send data in body; used for forms that change data), PUT (replace), DELETE, HEAD (headers only), PATCH, OPTIONS.
- **Status classes**: 1xx informational, 2xx success (200 OK, 201 Created), 3xx redirection (301 Moved Permanently, 302 Found, 304 Not Modified), 4xx client error (400 Bad Request, 401 Unauthorized, 403 Forbidden, 404 Not Found), 5xx server error (500 Internal Server Error, 503 Service Unavailable).
- **Static page**: same file sent to everyone. **Dynamic page**: generated per request by server-side code (PHP, ASP.NET, JSP/Servlets, Node.js, Python).

sections.heading: Web servers, hosting and the webmaster
sections.body:
A **web server** is software (and the machine running it) that accepts HTTP requests and serves resources.
- **Apache HTTP Server** - open source, from the Apache Software Foundation; modules such as `mod_rewrite`; configuration in `httpd.conf` / `.htaccess`.
- **Nginx** - open-source, event-driven, popular as reverse proxy and load balancer.
- **Microsoft IIS** (Internet Information Services) - Windows server, hosts ASP.NET applications.
- **Apache Tomcat** - servlet/JSP container for Java web applications.
- **LAMP** stack = Linux + Apache + MySQL + PHP/Perl/Python; **WAMP** uses Windows. PHP, Apache, MySQL and Linux are all open-source software.

**Web hosting** means renting space and bandwidth on an Internet-connected server:
- **Shared hosting** - many sites on one server; cheapest, least control.
- **VPS** (Virtual Private Server) - a virtual machine slice with dedicated resources.
- **Dedicated hosting** - a whole physical server for one customer.
- **Cloud hosting** - resources drawn from a cluster; scalable, pay-per-use.
- **Colocation** - you own the server, the data centre provides power, cooling and network.

Publishing a site: register a **domain name** with a registrar, point DNS to the host, upload files (FTP/SFTP or a control panel), and secure it with an SSL/TLS certificate. The **webmaster** is the person who runs and maintains the web server and site (uptime, updates, security, logs); a **web designer** handles look and layout.

sections.heading: HTML basics: document structure and core tags
sections.body:
**HTML** (HyperText Markup Language) is a **markup language** that describes the structure of a page through **tags**; it is not a programming language and is processed by the **browser (client side)**. Tags are written in angle brackets; most have a start and end tag (`

...

`), while **empty (void) elements** have no end tag: `
`, `
`, ``, ``, ``, ``. HTML tag names are **not case-sensitive**. - `` is the container for information *about* the page: ``, `<meta>`, `<link>`, `<style>`, `<script>`, `<base>`. `<body>` holds visible content. - **Headings**: six levels, `<h1>` (largest) to `<h6>` (smallest). - **Comment**: `<!-- comment -->` (not displayed, cannot be nested). - `<br>` = line break; `<p>` = paragraph; `<hr>` = horizontal rule; `<pre>` = preformatted text. - Text formatting: `<b>`/`<strong>`, `<i>`/`<em>`, `<u>`, `<sub>`, `<sup>`, `<mark>`. - **Links**: `<a href="url" target="_blank">`. **Images**: `<img src="a.png" alt="text" width height>`. - `<script>` embeds or links JavaScript; `<style>` holds internal CSS; `<link rel="stylesheet" href="x.css">` links external CSS. - Old (HTML 3.2/4) `<body>` attributes: `bgcolor`, `background`, `text`, `link` (unvisited link colour), `vlink` (**visited** link colour), `alink` (**active** link, the moment it is being clicked). - Old `<hr>` attributes: `align`, `size` (thickness), `width`, `noshade` (there is no `shade` attribute). - **Global attributes** usable on any element: `id`, `class` (one or more class names referring to style-sheet classes), `style`, `title`, `lang`, `hidden`, `data-*`.

sections.heading: HTML lists, tables, forms and HTML5
sections.body:
**Lists**: `<ul>` unordered (bullets), `<ol>` ordered (`type="1|A|a|I|i"`, `start="5"`), `<li>` items; `<dl>` description list with `<dt>` term and `<dd>` description.

**Tables**: `<table>`, `<tr>` row, `<th>` header cell (bold, centred by default), `<td>` data cell, `<caption>`, `<thead>`, `<tbody>`, `<tfoot>`. `colspan` merges cells across columns, `rowspan` down rows. `<colgroup>`/`<col>` group columns, and their `span` attribute gives the **number of columns** in the group. Old attributes: `border`, `cellpadding` (space inside a cell), `cellspacing` (space between cells).

**Forms**: `<form action="url" method="get|post">` with `<input type="text|password|radio|checkbox|submit|reset|file|hidden|email|number|date">`, `<textarea>`, `<select>`/`<option>`, `<button>`, `<label>`. Radio buttons with the same `name` allow one choice; checkboxes allow many.

**Frames**: `<frameset>`/`<frame>` are obsolete; `<iframe>` embeds another page inline.

**HTML5** (doctype `<!DOCTYPE html>`): semantic elements `<header>`, `<nav>`, `<section>`, `<article>`, `<aside>`, `<footer>`, `<main>`, `<figure>`; media `<audio>`, `<video>`; graphics `<canvas>` (script-drawn bitmap) and `<svg>`; new input types; APIs such as **Geolocation** (lets the user share location with sites they trust, only after permission), Web Storage (`localStorage`, `sessionStorage`), drag-and-drop and Web Workers. Java **applets** (Java programs embedded in a page and run by a Java-capable browser through `<applet>`) are obsolete and unsupported by modern browsers.

sections.heading: CSS: syntax, selectors and the cascade
sections.body:
**CSS** (Cascading Style Sheets) separates presentation from structure. A rule is `selector { property: value; }`.

Three ways to apply CSS, from highest to lowest normal priority: **inline** (`style="..."` attribute) > **internal/embedded** (`<style>` in head) > **external** (`.css` file via `<link>`). In practice internal and external rules compete by specificity and source order.

**Selectors**: element `p`, class `.note`, id `#menu`, universal `*`, group `h1, h2`, descendant `div p`, child `div > p`, adjacent sibling `h1 + p`, attribute `input[type="text"]`, pseudo-class `a:hover`, `li:first-child`, pseudo-element `p::first-line`, `::before`.

**Cascade order**: importance (`!important`), then **specificity**, then **source order** (later wins). Specificity is counted as (inline, IDs, classes/attributes/pseudo-classes, elements/pseudo-elements); often written as weights 1000/100/10/1.

**Inheritance**: text properties (`color`, `font-*`, `line-height`) inherit; box properties (`margin`, `padding`, `border`, `width`) do not.

sections.heading: CSS properties, box model, colours and layout
sections.body:
**Font and text**: `font-family`, `font-size`, `font-style` (normal/italic/oblique), **`font-weight`** (how bold: `normal` = 400, `bold` = 700, values 100-900), `font-variant`, shorthand `font`; `text-align`, `text-decoration`, `text-transform`, `line-height`, `letter-spacing`.

**Lists**: `list-style-type`, `list-style-image`, `list-style-position`; the shorthand **`list-style`** sets all three at once.

**Colours**: named (`red`), hexadecimal `#RRGGBB` (`#ff0000`), `rgb(255,0,0)`, `rgba()` with alpha (0 transparent to 1 opaque), **`hsl(hue 0-360°, saturation %, lightness %)`**, `hsla()`.

**Box model** (inside out): content → padding → border → margin. With the default `box-sizing: content-box`, `width` is only the content; with `border-box`, width includes padding and border.

**Units**: absolute `px`, `pt`, `cm`; relative `%`, `em` (parent font size), `rem` (root font size), `vw`/`vh` (1% of viewport).

**Positioning**: `static` (default), `relative` (offset from normal place), `absolute` (relative to nearest positioned ancestor), `fixed` (relative to viewport), `sticky`. `z-index` sets stacking. `display`: block, inline, inline-block, none, **flex** (one-dimensional layout), **grid** (two-dimensional). `visibility: hidden` hides but keeps space; `display: none` removes it. **Media queries** (`@media (max-width: 600px)`) give responsive design.

sections.heading: JavaScript fundamentals
sections.body:
**JavaScript** is a lightweight, interpreted (JIT-compiled in modern engines), **dynamically typed**, prototype-based scripting language standardised as **ECMAScript**. It runs mainly in the **browser (client side)** to make pages dynamic, and on servers through **Node.js**. It is unrelated to Java apart from the name. It is embedded with `<script>...</script>` or `<script src="app.js">`.

- Variables: `var` (function-scoped, hoisted), `let` and `const` (block-scoped).
- Primitive types: number, string, boolean, undefined, null, bigint, symbol; everything else is an object (arrays and functions are objects). `typeof null` returns `"object"` (a historic quirk).
- `==` compares after type conversion; `===` compares value **and** type.
- `+` with a string concatenates; `-`, `*`, `/` convert strings to numbers.
- Dialog boxes: `alert()` (message), `confirm()` (OK/Cancel → true/false), `prompt()` (returns input string or null).
- **DOM** (Document Object Model): the page as a tree of objects. Access via `document.getElementById()`, `getElementsByClassName()`, `querySelector()`; change content with `innerHTML` / `textContent`, style with `element.style.color`.
- **AJAX** (Asynchronous JavaScript and XML): updating part of a page by requesting data in the background (`XMLHttpRequest` or `fetch()`), without reloading the page; data is now usually JSON.

sections.heading: JavaScript event model
sections.body:
An **event** is something that happens to an element (click, key press, page load). Events give a page its **dynamic, interactive** behaviour. A handler can be attached in three ways:
- HTML attribute: `<button onclick="go()">`
- DOM property: `btn.onclick = go;` (only one handler per event)
- **`addEventListener(type, handler, useCapture)`** - many handlers allowed; removed with `removeEventListener`.

**Event flow (DOM Level 2)** has three phases: **capturing** (window → down to the target's parent), **target**, and **bubbling** (target → back up to window). By default listeners run in the **bubbling** phase; pass `true` (or `{capture: true}`) to listen during capture. `event.stopPropagation()` stops further propagation; `event.preventDefault()` cancels the default action (e.g. stop a form submitting or a link navigating). `event.target` is the element that triggered the event; `this`/`currentTarget` is the element whose handler is running. **Event delegation** puts one listener on a parent and uses `event.target` to handle many children.

sections.heading: XML: rules and well-formedness
sections.body: **XML** (eXtensible Markup Language, a W3C standard derived from **SGML**) is designed to **store and transport data**, while HTML displays it. XML has **no predefined tags**: authors define their own. It is text-based and platform-independent. **Well-formed XML rules**: - Exactly **one root element**. - Every element must be **closed** (`` or ``), and elements must be **properly nested**. - Tags are **case-sensitive** (`` ≠ ``). - Attribute values must be **quoted**. - **Element names** must start with a letter or underscore, may contain letters, digits, hyphens, underscores and periods, **cannot contain spaces**, and **must not start with "xml"** (in any case), which is reserved. - Special characters use entities: `<` `>` `&` `'` `"`. - Comments: `` (may span several lines, cannot contain `--`). `` holds text that is not parsed. - Optional prolog: ``. A document is **well-formed** if it obeys the syntax rules; it is **valid** if it is well-formed **and** conforms to a DTD or schema. Every valid document is well-formed, not vice versa. Related technologies: **XSLT** (transform XML), **XPath** (navigate/select nodes), **XQuery**, **XML namespaces** (avoid name conflicts), **XHTML** (HTML reformulated as XML).

sections.heading: DTD, XML Schema and XML parsers
sections.body:
A **DTD** (Document Type Definition) declares the legal elements, attributes and entities of a document; DTDs originate from SGML. It can be **internal** (inside `<!DOCTYPE root [ ... ]>`) or **external** (`<!DOCTYPE root SYSTEM "file.dtd">`).
- `<!ELEMENT name (child1, child2)>` - sequence; `|` choice; `?` zero or one; `*` zero or more; `+` one or more; `(#PCDATA)` parsed character data; `EMPTY`; `ANY`.
- `<!ATTLIST elem attr CDATA #REQUIRED>` - defaults `#REQUIRED`, `#IMPLIED` (optional), `#FIXED "value"`, or a default literal; types CDATA, ID, IDREF, enumerated.
- `<!ENTITY name "text">` used as `&name;`.

**XML Schema (XSD)** is itself written in XML, supports **data types** (xs:string, xs:integer, xs:date), namespaces and min/max occurrence; a DTD has no real data types and is not XML syntax.

**Parsers**:
- **DOM parser** - loads the whole document into an in-memory **tree**; random access, can modify; memory-heavy for large files.
- **SAX** (Simple API for XML) - **event-driven**, reads sequentially, fires callbacks (startElement, endElement, characters); fast and low-memory, read-only, no going back.
- **StAX** - pull parser (application pulls events).
- **Validating** parsers check against DTD/XSD; **non-validating** ones check only well-formedness.

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<!DOCTYPE library [
  <!ELEMENT library (book+)>
  <!ELEMENT book (title, author*)>

  <!ATTLIST book isbn CDATA #REQUIRED lang CDATA "en">
]>

</library>

sections.heading: Front-end tools and libraries
sections.body:
**Front-end** (client side) = what runs in the browser: **HTML, CSS, JavaScript** and tools built on them. **Back-end** = server, application logic and database (PHP, Java, Python, Node.js, SQL/PL-SQL). PL/SQL is a database language, not a front-end technology.

- **JavaScript libraries**: **React** (component-based UI library from Meta, virtual DOM, JSX), **jQuery** (DOM manipulation, `$()` selector, AJAX helpers).
- **Frameworks**: Angular (Google, TypeScript), Vue.js; CSS frameworks **Bootstrap** (grid, ready components) and **Tailwind CSS** (utility-first classes).
- **Front-end assets**: icon sets such as **Font Awesome**, web fonts, images.
- **Boilerplates / starting points**: HTML5 Boilerplate, **Reset CSS** / Normalize.css (remove browser default style differences).
- Tooling: npm (package manager), bundlers (Webpack, Vite), preprocessors (Sass/SCSS, Less), TypeScript (typed superset of JS), browser DevTools for debugging.
- **Responsive design**: fluid grids, flexible images and media queries so one site fits phones and desktops.

sections.heading: Microsoft .NET, ASP.NET and VB.NET
sections.body:
**.NET** is Microsoft's developer platform. The original **.NET Framework** is Windows-only; modern **.NET** (successor of .NET Core) is **free, open-source and cross-platform** (Windows, Linux, macOS, plus mobile through other workloads).

Compilation path: source (C#, VB.NET, F#) → language compiler → **CIL/MSIL** (Common Intermediate Language: CPU-independent, machine-language-style instruction set) stored in an **assembly** (.exe/.dll with metadata and manifest) → **JIT compiler** inside the CLR converts IL to native code at run time. **NGen** pre-compiles IL to native ahead of time.

- **CLR** (Common Language Runtime) - the virtual machine (execution engine): JIT compilation, memory management and **garbage collection**, type safety, exception handling, security. Code run by it is **managed code**.
- **CTS** (Common Type System) - defines types all .NET languages share; **CLS** (Common Language Specification) - the subset of rules for language interoperability, enabling cross-language inheritance.
- **FCL/BCL** - Framework/Base Class Library.
- **.NET languages**: C#, VB.NET, F#, C++/CLI, J# (discontinued). Classic Pascal is not a .NET language.
- **ASP.NET** - server-side web framework (Web Forms with server controls, ViewState and postback; MVC; Web API; Razor Pages). **Data binding** connects controls to a data source for read/write display. **ADO.NET** - data access (Connection, Command, DataReader, DataAdapter, DataSet). **ASP.NET AJAX** (ScriptManager, UpdatePanel) gives partial-page updates.
- **WPF** = Windows Presentation Foundation (desktop UI using XAML); **WCF** = Windows Communication Foundation (services); **WinForms** = classic desktop forms.
- **VB.NET** is a fully object-oriented language on .NET; it is **not** a subset of, nor fully compatible with, Visual Basic 6. Example keyword: `Append` (`OpenMode.Append`) is the file-open mode constant used with `FileOpen`.

formulas.name: CSS specificity
formulas.note: Compare left to right; equal specificity → later rule wins; !important overrides normal rules.

formulas.name: Box width (content-box)
formulas.formula: Total width = width + 2×padding + 2×border (+ 2×margin for space occupied)
formulas.note: With box-sizing: border-box, width already includes padding and border.

formulas.name: URL structure
formulas.note: Default port 80 for http, 443 for https.

formulas.name: rem / em
formulas.formula: 1rem = root font size; 1em = font size of the element's parent (for font-size)
formulas.note: Default browser root size is usually 16px.

workedExamples.problem: Which rule colours the link? Rule 1: `#nav .item a { color: red }`  Rule 2: `div ul li a.active { color: blue }`. Both match the same link.
workedExamples.solution:
Count specificity as (ids, classes, elements):
- Rule 1: one id (#nav), one class (.item), one element (a) → (1, 1, 1).
- Rule 2: no id, one class (.active), four elements (div, ul, li, a) → (0, 1, 4).
Compare from the left: ids 1 > 0, so Rule 1 wins regardless of the element count.
**Answer: red.** One id outweighs any number of classes or elements.

workedExamples.problem: A div has `width: 200px; padding: 10px; border: 5px solid; margin: 20px`. Find (a) its visible width with content-box, (b) the horizontal space it occupies, (c) the content width if `box-sizing: border-box`.
workedExamples.solution:
(a) Visible width = content + left/right padding + left/right border = 200 + 2×10 + 2×5 = **230 px**.
(b) Add margins: 230 + 2×20 = **270 px**.
(c) With border-box the 200 px already includes padding and border, so content = 200 − 20 − 10 = **170 px**.

workedExamples.problem: Find all well-formedness errors: `<?xml version="1.0"?> <1st-list><item id=5>Pen</Item><item>Ink</list>`
workedExamples.solution:
1. Name `1st-list` starts with a digit - element names must start with a letter or underscore.
2. Attribute value `5` is not quoted - must be `id="5"`.
3. `<item>` is closed by `</Item>` - XML is case-sensitive, so the tags do not match.
4. The second `<item>` is never closed, so nesting is broken.
5. The end tag `</list>` does not match the root start tag `<1st-list>`.
Corrected: `<list1><item id="5">Pen</item><item>Ink</item></list1>`.

workedExamples.problem: A `<button id="b">` sits inside `<div id="d">`. Handlers: `d.addEventListener('click', A)`, `b.addEventListener('click', B)`, `d.addEventListener('click', C, true)`. In what order do A, B, C run when the button is clicked?
workedExamples.solution:
Event flow: capturing phase (top → down), then target, then bubbling (bottom → up).
- C is registered on the div with `useCapture = true`, so it runs while the event travels down: **C** first.
- At the target (button): **B**.
- Bubbling back up to the div: **A** (default listeners use the bubbling phase).
**Order: C, B, A.** If B called `event.stopPropagation()`, A would not run.

workedExamples.problem: A table must show a title cell across all 3 columns in row 1, and in rows 2-3 a cell 'Total' spanning both rows in the first column. How many `<td>` tags are written in rows 1, 2 and 3?
workedExamples.solution:
- Row 1: one cell with `colspan="3"` → **1** tag.
- Row 2: the 'Total' cell with `rowspan="2"` + 2 normal cells → **3** tags.
- Row 3: column 1 is already occupied by the rowspan cell, so only **2** tags.
Total = 1 + 3 + 2 = 6 cell tags for a 3×3 grid (9 positions): the colspan cell covers 3 positions and the rowspan cell covers 2.

pitfalls: VLINK = colour of a visited link; ALINK = colour while the link is being clicked (active); LINK = unvisited link.
HTML has 6 heading levels (h1-h6), not 7; h1 is the largest.
`<head>` is the container for page information (title, meta); `<title>` is only one element inside it.
`span` on `<col>/<colgroup>` = number of columns in the group; `colspan` is for a single cell.
HTML is a markup language processed in the browser - it is not server-side and not a programming language.
XML is case-sensitive; HTML tag names are not. XML element names cannot start with a digit or with 'xml'.
A valid XML document must be well-formed, but a well-formed document need not be valid.
DTD has no data types; XML Schema does. SAX is event-based and read-only; DOM builds the whole tree in memory.
font-weight controls boldness; font-style controls italic. `list-style` is the shorthand, not list-style-type.
AJAX = Asynchronous JavaScript and XML (not 'Associated', not 'HTML').
VB.NET is not a subset of VB 6.0; CIL/MSIL is CPU-independent and converted to native code by the JIT inside the CLR.
